_comment: Hand-written prose keyed by node / edge / flow id. NEVER overwritten by the generator — it merges these in on every run. Put explanation HERE, not in architecture.json. Keys matching no node/edge/flow are reported as orphanAnnotations (usually a rename).
flow.weekly-scoring: The most defensive path in the codebase, and the reason it is defensive is that league_standings increments are irreversible. There is no transaction around the read-then-increment and no compensating write, so a fabricated score cannot be undone by re-running. Three guards therefore refuse rather than guess. Read them in order: decideBatchScoring kills a whole snapshot-less league-week; decideUserScorer marks an individual snapshot-less user unscoreable past week 1; decideMatchupScoring refuses any matchup containing one. All three exist because the fallback scorer returns cumulative-from-draft-entry P/L, which is only a valid weekly delta in week 1.
flow.week-end-snapshot: Read this against flow.week-start-snapshot — the asymmetry is the point. snapshot-week-start has an extracted, unit-tested plan.ts and was hardened in 2caf9f8 to write all-or-nothing per league-week with a completeness-based skip. snapshot-week-end has neither: no extracted module, no tests, and its write path has not been audited for the same partial-write defect. Both feed the same week_snapshots rows that weekly scoring reads, and week-end runs only ten minutes before scoring does.
flow.season-reset: The only flow where a destructive operation is authorized entirely inside a function body. EXECUTE on start_new_league_season is granted to `authenticated`, so any logged-in user can call it with any league id. Nothing in the grant layer stops a non-commissioner from resetting someone else's league — the internal commissioner check is the whole control. That is deliberate (the client calls it directly, so it must be authenticated-callable), but it means the gate has to be correct, with no defence in depth if it regresses.
flow.place-trade:
The trade row is written by the client, not by place-order. place-order reads broker_credentials, submits to Alpaca, and returns; TradeModal then inserts into trades. The broker order and the database record are committed by two different actors with nothing linking them transactionally, so a crash, network drop, or backgrounded app between the two leaves a real position at Alpaca with no row in the DB. flow.order-reconciliation exists to close that window after the fact.

PARTIAL SALES READ AS A BUG BUT ARE NOT ONE. If a position is partly sold during the week, the matchup and dashboard screens show UNREALIZED P/L on the quantity still held at week end, while the scorer additionally settles the REALIZED P/L of the sold portion from midWeekTrades. So a screen and a standings number can legitimately differ after a partial sale, and the screen will read low. This is pre-existing and symmetrical: week-start holdings behave the same way, because their snapshot quantity is Monday's and the UI never consults trades. Not a defect — but it is the first thing a user will report, so recognise it rather than re-investigating.
fn.process-week-results:
1481 lines, and the only production caller is one cron job. Runs with verify_jwt=false, so the in-code constant-time apikey check is the entire authentication boundary — note it runs before the body parse and before the DB client is constructed, which is what makes an unauthenticated request cheap to reject. The two extracted modules are the parts that have been burned by bugs and are now pinned by hermetic unit tests.

STRANDED STATUS ROWS (traced 2026-07-27). It writes 'running' to cron_job_status at index.ts:851, but terminal statuses exist at only two places: 'success' at :1463 and 'failed' at :1477. Two returns sit between them and write NEITHER, leaving the row permanently at 'running':
  - :890 — no pending matchups. Returns HTTP 200, logs 'No pending matchups to process'. This is the common path.
  - :885 — the matchup query itself failed. Returns HTTP 500, logs 'Error fetching matchups:'.
Discriminate the two by status code or by that log line. The three returns before :851 (:819 apikey rejected, :832 missing config) write no row at all, which is a different and less confusing state. :1311 and :1325 are returns inside the nested updateUserStandings helper, not handler returns.

NOT A SCORING OUTAGE. Five consecutive Fridays (2026-06-26 through 07-24) sat at 'running'. `unscored` was confirmed 0 across every league — no matchups with team1_gain IS NULL and week_end < now() — so :890 firing weekly is the function correctly reporting there is nothing to score. The stranded row is the entire finding. Do not read those five rows as five missed scoring runs.

See CLAUDE.md silent-failure #6 for why this shape is worse than a merely wrong signal.
fn.snapshot-week-start:
Modernised in 2caf9f8: all-or-nothing writes per league-week, with a completeness-based coverage gate that runs BEFORE any Alpaca call and skips on alreadyEndPriced / none_expected / complete, healing only the missing participants when coverage is partial.

READ THE 'will retry' LOG WITH SUSPICION. The ABORT path at index.ts:466 refuses a partial snapshot and logs '... refusing partial snapshot, will retry'. That promise has never been kept: schedule_snapshot_retry passes a TIMESTAMPTZ to cron.schedule, which has no such overload, so it raises on every call and no retry has ever been scheduled in this database. The all-or-nothing REFUSAL is live; its RECOVERY is not. An aborted league writes nothing and waits for the next Mon/Tue cron rather than re-attempting in 5 minutes. Fix drafted at supabase/migrations/20260727000000_fix_schedule_snapshot_retry_cron_expression.sql on branch fix/schedule-snapshot-retry-cron-expression — UNPUSHED as of 2026-07-27. Until it lands, treat that log line as an intention, not a guarantee.

ZERO WRITES IS OFTEN CORRECT. Paths producing no week_snapshots rows: :302 Monday holiday (early return, loop never runs), :324 no active matchup leagues, :357 no matchups for the league-week, :413 already_end_priced, :420 no_holdings, :425 already_complete. The two that indicate a PROBLEM are :466 (abort, unpriced symbols) and :494 (upsert error) — and both set anyIncomplete, which forces status 'retrying' (:516) or 'failed' (:530). So terminal status 'success' at :540 PROVES neither problem path fired. Zero rows plus 'success' means every league hit a benign skip.

One trap in that list: :302 depends on isMarketOpenToday, which returns open:false on a 401 (CLAUDE.md silent-failure #1). A stale Alpaca key therefore produces 'success' + zero rows + the log line 'Monday is a market holiday, skipping' on a day that is not a holiday.
fn.snapshot-week-end: The unmodernised twin of snapshot-week-start. Same cron-auth pattern, same Alpaca dependency, same table — but no extracted pure module and no test file. It is the highest-value cleanup target in the repo precisely because its failure mode is silent: bad week_end_price data does not throw, it just scores people wrong.
mod.process-week-results/grouping: The batch key is (league_id, week_number), not league_id. Grouping by league alone meant a league with several unscored weeks scored every one of them against week[0]'s snapshots and trade window. The sort order is equally load-bearing: the handler advances current_week only when the batch's week equals the league's current week, so weeks must arrive ascending or a league gets permanently stuck.
mod.process-week-results/scoring-eligibi: Pure decision functions — no side effects, no Deno APIs; every logging call and DB write stays in index.ts. The evaluation ORDER inside decideBatchScoring is part of the contract: freshness is checked before the week>1 rule, so a stale week>1 batch reports stale_no_snapshots (the actionable operational cause) rather than the generic reason. Swapping them would silently relabel every stale skip.
pg.start_new_league_season: Destructive (deletes and recreates season state) and callable by any authenticated user. anon was revoked in 20260718000000; `authenticated` was deliberately kept because the mobile client calls it directly. Authorization is therefore entirely the internal commissioner check.
pg.join_league_by_code: EXECUTE is service_role only, which is the correct shape: the client never calls it, the join-league edge function does, and that function passes the JWT-verified user id rather than anything from the request body. An earlier version was authenticated-callable with a forgeable p_user_id.
tbl.league_standings: Written by read-then-increment with no transaction and no idempotency key. This is the single most important fact about the scoring path — it is why process-week-results refuses to score rather than risk a wrong number, and why a re-run is safe only because the top-level query re-selects on team1_gain IS NULL.
tbl.cron_job_status:
The ops table three cron functions write, with UNIQUE(job_name, run_date) and run_date defaulting to CURRENT_DATE — so each job gets exactly one row per day and every write is an upsert onto it.

Do NOT treat this table as a reliable health signal. process-week-results writes 'running' and, on its two most likely returns (index.ts:890 and :885), never writes a terminal status — so a row reading 'running' is byte-identical whether the function hung, crashed mid-run, or completed normally with nothing to do. snapshot-week-start and snapshot-week-end DO write terminal statuses on every path, so their rows are trustworthy; process-week-results' are not. Any alerting built on this table must account for that asymmetry or it will either fire every week or never fire at all.

Also note the upsert semantics when testing by hand: calling schedule_snapshot_retry directly OVERWRITES the day's real row for that job rather than inserting a new one.
pg.schedule_snapshot_retry:
FIXED and verified 2026-07-27. For its entire life until then it had never scheduled a retry: it declared retry_time TIMESTAMPTZ and passed it to cron.schedule, which has only (schedule text, command text) and (job_name text, schedule text, command text) overloads — and PostgreSQL removed implicit datetime->text casts in 8.3, so the call resolved to nothing and raised on every invocation.

It survived three migrations looking healthy because PL/pgSQL resolves called-function names at EXECUTION time, not at CREATE FUNCTION time — a migration applying cleanly says nothing about whether its function bodies work. And it left no trace because the INSERT INTO cron_job_status ... 'retrying' sits AFTER the PERFORM and a function body is atomic, so the raise rolled back its own evidence.

The fix passes a five-field cron expression formatted from the retry instant in cron.timezone. Proven live: calling it returned without error (it previously raised) and wrote a 'retrying' row — THE FIRST that table has ever held. That row is the evidence; before the fix the query for it could only ever return zero rows.

Note the change is BEHAVIOR-ADDING. MAX_RETRIES is 3 in both callers and the initial run counts as attempt 1, so a failing run can now re-invoke its function up to 2 more times. For snapshot-week-start that is safe and useful — the coverage gate skips complete leagues and heals only missing participants. For snapshot-week-end it is safe but INEFFECTIVE: its existence-only alreadyProcessed guard skips a league as soon as ANY row carries a week_end_price, so a retry cannot heal a partial week-end write.
tbl.rate_limit_counters: RLS on with zero policies is intentional — it denies every client role outright, and only service_role (which bypasses RLS) touches the table via check_and_bump_rate_limit. Flagged as low-severity drift for inventory completeness, not as a defect.
cron.refresh_symbols_daily: The oldest job in the schedule (jobid 7, versus 18-21 for the cron-auth-migrated set) and the only one that sends no auth header at all. It predates the RLS-hardening pass that set verify_jwt=true on refresh-symbols, and it was never migrated because no migration in the repo schedules it — it was created out-of-band, so the Phase 2b sweep over supabase/migrations/ never saw it. Its `symbols` target table is likewise created by no migration. IMPORTANT when diagnosing this: cron.job_run_details reports 'succeeded' for every run regardless, because net.http_post is asynchronous — the job status records that the request was ENQUEUED (return_message '1 row' is the request id), not what the server answered. Checked 2026-07-27: five consecutive 'succeeded' runs, which is exactly what a job 401ing every six hours also looks like. Use net._http_response, or check whether the symbols rows actually changed.
e.ui.league-settings->pg.start_new_leagu: The only direct client-to-SECURITY-DEFINER call in the app. Every other definer function is reached through an edge function.
e.fn.process-week-results->tbl.league_st: Read, add, write back. Two concurrent runs would double-count; in practice only one cron job triggers this, but nothing in the schema enforces that.
tbl.week_snapshots:
One row per (league, user, week, symbol) — the unique constraint is what makes the snapshot writes idempotent and safe against overlapping retries.

week_start_price is NOT NULL and always has been. Until 2026-07-27 snapshot-week-end tried to insert NULL into it for mid-week purchases, so that insert failed on every run since 2026-01-15 and those positions were silently dropped from scoring — not merely missing a row, but scored wrong, since calculateUserScore drops a mid-week buy with no end price from BOTH totalGain and totalStartValue.

entered_mid_week is now the discriminator. week_start_price on such a row is the purchase entry price, NOT a Monday open. Both scorers key on the flag, never on the price being null — keying on the price would treat the row as a week-start holding and double-count it, because the same buy is already carried in midWeekTrades. The three UI surfaces that multiply quantity * week_start_price for cost basis need no flag: they compute (currentPrice - entryPrice) * quantity, which is correct for both row kinds.
